newsitem.title: UK: Boots Q3 sales rise six percent.
newsitem.headline: Boots Q3 sales rise six percent.

text.p: UK retailer and chemist Boots Co Plc on Monday said comparable sales rose six percent in the quarter to the end of December 1996.
Like-for-like sales at Boots The Chemist rose 5.1 percent.
Deputy chairman and chief executive Lord Blyth said the group's overall performance was satisfactory, but Christmas sales were slow in December.
"Although the Christmas season began well, sales were slow through December until a surge in the final few days which has continued into the first part of January," he said in a statement.

Health and beauty sales were strong, with beauty and personal care products up nine percent. Cosmetics, including own brand No 7 and 17, rose by more than 20 percent. Healthcare sales were up eight percent, despite the relative absence of flu before Christmas.

Car accessory business Halfords suffered a three percent like for like sales decline, due to lower sales of cycles and "delayed sales of winter products." Boots said sales had improved with the onset of the cold weather.

Boots Opticians boosted sales by 12.2 percent. Home improvement chain Do It All achieved a 7.3 percent increase in like for like sales from its 133 active stores. A.G. Stanley, the home decorating business, saw like for like sales rise 0.4 percent. A.G. Stanley's Homestyle out of town stores increase sales by 7.5 percent, but this was offset by a drop of 10.8 percent in FADS, where 11 stores were closed.
Boots said increased incidence of flu had boosted healthcare sales by more than 20 percent in the first week of the fourth quarter trading period.
In the third quarter, sales of over-the-counter medicines outstripped those prescribed by doctors for the first time, the company said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
